title: Thistle & Reeve — partnership playbook (scratch)
content:
Quick working notes for Thistle & Reeve (T&R) — internal scratchpad. NOT FOR CUSTOMER.

Context / why we're chasing
- T&R is a mid-market B2B marketplace for boutique hotels; recent Series B (Nov 2024 rumour). Heavy personalization and search needs on product pages.
- Heard via partner signal (ref from CSM @ BlueHarbor) that they are exploring in-house LLM for guest messaging and dynamic recommendations.
- Key pain: latency spikes during booking peak windows -> dropped conversions. Also concerned about inference cost as scale grows.

High-level thesis (one-liner)
- Redwood Inference can reduce token cost and tail latency via dedicated reserved pools + caching + quantized model variants while giving them control (VPC/private) for PII-sensitive messaging.

Top contacts (LinkedIn / notes)
- Maya Feld (Head of Product) — leads personalization + search. (maya@thistle-reeve.com)
- Rajiv Chauhan (Sr. Eng, Platform) — owns infra and vendor evaluations. (rajiv@tr.com)
- Olivia Park (Growth lead) — cares about conversion metrics and A/Bs.
- Intro path: Maya -> Olivia -> Rajiv for tech eval.

Quick company signals
- Careers: hiring ML infra and SRE (good signal: budget + care about infra).
- Tech stack: AWS + EKS, Postgres, ~React front-end. They run Redis for caching.
- Privacy: listed SOC2 on careers page; likely to prioritize auditability.

Technical fit notes
- Use-cases: chat/reservation assistant (low-latency), personalized ranking (embeddings + reranking), template generation for guest messages (sensitive content).
- Requirements we can meet: private deployment (VPC + customer KMS), dedicated reserved capacity for steady throughput, prefix KV cache for common prompts, intelligent batching for offline rerank jobs.
- Potential friction: they mention need for <60ms 95p on short-turn assistant queries. That is aggressive but achievable with optimized kernels and regional routing (need to confirm target region).

Preliminary numbers (from quick ask to them — to verify)
- Concurrent assistant QPS: 40–80 during peak (est).
- Average prompt length: 120 tokens; response 80 tokens.
- Monthly active users: 210k (growth).
- Pilot target: reduce cost-per-conversation by 30% and 95p latency <120ms. (stretch goal: 60ms)

Pilot proposal (30 day) — draft to test
- Scope: production-like pilot on Dedicated (small pool: 2x A10G equiv) serving a subset of assistant traffic (10% routing) + offline rerank job for 1k queries/day.
- Success metrics: 30% unit cost reduction vs current provider (ask them for invoice), 99.5% pilot uptime, no data exfil claims, 90% of assistant requests under 120ms 95p.
- Deliverables: deployment topology doc, runbook for failover (fallback to hosted model), end-of-pilot cost/latency report + suggested rollout plan.
- Pricing ask: propose 1-month trial credit covering infra + 50% discount on first 3 months of Dedicated base. (Internal: check with pricing team)

Outbound sequence (cold -> follow ups)
- Subject line options: "Personalization latency at Thistle & Reeve" / "Quick idea to lower convo cost by 30%"
- Cold email (short):
  Hi Maya —
  Quick note: I saw T&R is growing personalization + messaging. We work with marketplaces to cut inference cost and tail latency while keeping control over customer data (VPC/KMS). Could we share a 15-min note on whether you’re evaluating infra for chat/rerank?
  — Emma (Redwood)
- Follow-up #1 (3 days): add a one-sentence proof point: "Reduced tail latency to ~90ms 95p for a hospitality client serving similar QPS" and a calendar link.
- Follow-up #2 (1 week): share a one-pager (attach) with pilot outline and SLA bullets.
- Breakup note (after 3 attempts): "If timing's off, who on your team owns this? Happy to send a brief pilot plan."

Call prep checklist (for intro call with Maya)
- Ask: what are current latency and cost per convo; monthly invoice range for LLM infra?
- Ask: where does sensitive PII live (postgres vs 3p forms) and what compliance auditors do they care about?
- Demo: show per-route token-level cost and console tracing -> how we isolate assistant route and show cost win.
- Bring: sample pilot topology + fallback plan + SSO/KMS notes.

Objection handling (short bullets)
- Security / data residency: highlight Private deploy (VPC + customer KMS + optional on-prem). Offer SOC2 report and customer references.
- Latency target too tight: propose hybrid routing — dedicated for assistant, hosted edge fallback for sporadic bursts. Also measure real distribution in pilot.
- Cost savings claim skepticism: include before/after examples and a breakdown (batching, quantization, cache hit rate). Offer access to a small baseline run to show delta.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: stress model-agnostic runtime + ability to pin model versions + export logs for audits.

Internal asks / next steps (notes to self)
- Connect with Solutions Eng: @Liam Ortiz for pilot topology + quick perf sims (deadline: 2024-11-25).
- Ask Pricing: what baseline trial credit is permissible for a mid-market pilot. (Priya)
- Jira: create INF-1890 with pilot scope + acceptance criteria. Link to Confluence PRJ-THISTLE-679.
- Prepare short one-pager specifically showing hospitality marketplace case study (lift + latency numbers).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve (quick list)
- Confirm region they want (us-east-1 vs eu-west-1).
- Exact 95p latency requirement: 60ms vs 120ms — need to clarify.
- Do they have model preferences (open weights vs managed models)?
- Where are credit card / PII flows stored — determines whether private deployment is required.

Notes to self (style/delivery)
- Keep initial outreach consultative (no price) — focus on measurable ops pain (latency + cost).
- Maya responds better to experiments (A/Bs), Olivia wants conversion uplift numbers.
- Rajiv will deep-dive on runtime/ops — prep kernel/quant notes and SLOs.

Draft outreach snippet for Olivia (Growth) — short product pitch
  Subject: "Convo lift during peak booking windows"
  Olivia —
  We ran a small dedicated pilot with a marketplace last quarter and cut 40% of per-conversation cost while improving tail latency through caching + reserved pools. Would love 10 mins to share the setup and what an A/B might look like for your booking flow.

Misc: quick copy fragments to reuse
- "reserved capacity + prefix caching to tame peaks"
- "VPC private control plane + customer KMS for sensitive messages"
- "drop-in runtime — keep models you want, serve with lower unit economics"

TODO
- [ ] Book sync with Liam (SE)
- [ ] Create pilot Jira INF-1890 + assign acceptance criteria
- [ ] Draft one-pager + attach to follow-up email
- [ ] Get pricing sign-off for trial credit

End of scratchpad.

(If this looks promising, spin a customer-facing one-pager from the pilot section and hand to marketing for a hospitality specific collateral.)
